newsitem.title: USA: Jury selected for Army rape case.
newsitem.headline: Jury selected for Army rape case.

text.p: A six-member military jury has been selected for the court martial trial of Staff Sgt. Delmar Simpson, accused of raping six female trainees.
The jury, selected after a day and a half of questioning of 10 potential panellists by attorneys for both sides, is made up of one white woman, two black men and three white men.
"Given with what we started with, we're very satisfied," defence attorney Frank Spinner said at a news conference.

Simpson, 32, is charged with 19 counts of rape and 55 other instances of sexual misconduct and other crimes while serving as a drill instructor at the Aberdeen Proving Ground in Maryland beginning in 1995.
He pleaded guilty to 16 of those counts -- 11 of sexual intercourse with trainees and five of propositioning -- but pleaded innocent to rape and the other charges.
On Tuesday, prosecutors dropped 19 other charges against Simpson, including raping two women with whom he admitted having sex. Prosecutors gave no reason for the decision.

Prospective jurors were questioned on issues ranging from their exposure to media reports about the highly publicised case to their memories of their own military service and whether they thought drill instructors should be held to a higher standard.

The defence asked for two jurors to be removed. One said his wife had been a victim of date rape, the other said his wife knew Simpson and had a professional disagreement with him. Defence attorneys and prosecutors also exercised their right to strike one potential juror each without cause, leaving six for the panel.
Opening arguments are scheduled to begin Friday morning. Spinner said the defence would wait to decide whether Simpson takes the stand.
"If the government has failed to prove him guilty without a reasonable doubt, why should he take the stand?" he asked.

The Army's investigation into sexual misconduct at Aberdeen has drawn criticism that it may be racially biased given that all 10 trainers so far are black and most of their accusers are white. The Army has denied bias exists.

Simpson is the first of 10 soldiers charged in the military's biggest sex scandal since the Navy's 1991 Tailhook affair to go to trial, and he has been charged with the most crimes. Four other cases have been resolved through plea agreements or administrative proceedings.
